title: The Slower Process Pool
subtitle: Parallel work is slower than one process

brief.narrative: Tiny tasks send 20 MB Python objects to worker processes. Pickling, copying, and IPC cost more than the computation itself.
symptoms: Process Pool metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: Task granularity is too small relative to multiprocessing serialization and IPC overhead.
options.feedback: Correct. Multiprocessing bypasses the GIL but does not make communication free. Minimize data movement and bound worker count.

options.text: CPU oversubscription created scheduling and cache-locality overhead.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: The failure boundary is a process, not a thread; memory is isolated between processes.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: A data race on a non-atomic shared counter caused lost increments.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Size CPU-bound workers near the effective CPU quota, batch work, and measure run queue, throttling, switches, and throughput.

options.text: Run unsafe or CPU-heavy work in supervised worker processes and define IPC, restart, timeout, and idempotency behavior.
